name: Worcestershire
description: Worcestershire is a rural county in the West Midlands known for fertile farmland, orchards and the Malvern Hills. Worcester is the main city, while towns such as Redditch, Kidderminster and Evesham reflect the county's mix of historic, agricultural and industrial landscapes.

places.name: Worcester
places.description: A cathedral city on the River Severn in the West Midlands, best known for Worcester Cathedral, its porcelain-making heritage, and the nearby Battle of Worcester site that ended the English Civil War in 1651.

places.name: Bromsgrove
places.description: A market town district in Worcestershire on the edge of the West Midlands conurbation, known for the Avoncroft Museum of Historic Buildings and its role in the 19th-century needle and nail-making trades.

places.name: Malvern Hills
places.description: A district in Worcestershire named for its dramatic hill range, long associated with composer Edward Elgar and the source of Malvern spring water.

places.name: Redditch
places.description: A New Town in Worcestershire built up rapidly from the 1960s, though its older core has centuries of history as a world centre of needle manufacturing.

places.name: Wychavon
places.description: A rural district in Worcestershire covering the market town of Evesham and the Vale of Evesham, a major fruit and vegetable growing region.

places.name: Wyre Forest
places.description: A district in Worcestershire named for its ancient woodland, covering the Severn-side town of Bewdley and the resort town of Kidderminster, historically famous for carpet-weaving.
